title: Playing under guard during the Mau Mau fighting in the Congo
summary: On the 1959-60 tour, soldiers and bowmen ringed the hotel veranda where they played for dignitaries, so Bigard stayed behind the piano; he says the war stopped while Louie was there.

blocks.x: No, no. I'll think of it after a while as we go along. But so it wasn't for me. (Unintelligible)
What year was that tour?
The year we went to Africa?
Uh-huh.
What year was that?
'59 and part of '60.
You remember when the Mau Mau were killing all the people around there? And they had a war and when we got there, anyway, and it was --
Elizabethville.
-- Elizabethville and -- what's the other ville? There's another ville.
What was the name of the place?
Brazzaville. [Elizabethville and Leopoldville, P.B.]
That's in Ghana.
That's in Ghana.

So that night we had to play for the dignitaries at this hotel, but it was out on a huge veranda. So when we were getting out there, we see soldiers ringing around the veranda. I happened to look up and in the trees I see some natives up there with bow and arrows. So we played that first set and got off to relaxing and I asked a guy, I says, "What's all the soldiers and characters up in the tree with spears and bow and arrows?" He said, "Well, the Mau Maus was on a raid. So that's to protect the people here." I said, "Yeah?" I said, "You guys are expecting the Mau Mau?" He said, "Yeah." He said, "They may come anywhere." I said, "Fine. I'm glad you told me." So the rest of the evening I played behind the piano and I stayed behind the piano.
(Laughter.)
Believe me, I wouldn't come out from that piano.
And so we got through that all right. That went off fine.
Were you saying earlier that the war stopped when Louie got there?
What? Yeah, the war, they stopped the
* Brazzaville is in Congo.
war when Louie came. That's the truth. Both sides stopped fighting.
And then when Louie left they resumed?
Oh, yeah. When we left they went on.
